identification.summary: Storm-2981 is reportedly Microsoft's name (not independently verified in searches) for a financially motivated cluster that Microsoft's naming map lists with the alias Coinbase Cartel [S1]. Third-party vendors describe Coinbase Cartel as a data-theft-only extortion group that does not encrypt victim systems and that runs a Tor leak site [S2][S8]. The name carries no connection to the Coinbase exchange per vendor reporting; the Microsoft Storm-2981 to Coinbase Cartel mapping rests on the mapping file alone [S1].
identification.notes: Vendors report the leak site debuted on 15 September 2025 with roughly ten victim listings posted at once [S2]. One reporting item dates activity to September 2023, which conflicts with the other reports [S3]. Microsoft published no narrative report on Storm-2981 that was found in searches; all behavioral detail below comes from third-party vendors tracking Coinbase Cartel, so vendor cluster boundaries may not match Microsoft's [S1][S2].

attribution.sponsor: Non-state, financially motivated criminal extortion group; no state sponsor identified in cited sources [S1][S2].
attribution.confidence: Low to moderate on ecosystem links. CybelAngel states that Fortinet FortiGuard Labs and Halcyon link the group to the Scattered LAPSUS$ Hunters (SLSH) ecosystem [S2]; reporting on the Grafana incident repeats that Halcyon and FortiGuard assess it as an SLSH offshoot [S3]. These are vendor assessments, not government attribution.
attribution.basis: Vendor assessment based on shared contacts, infrastructure and tactics with the SLSH collective (ShinyHunters, Scattered Spider, Lapsus$) as reported by Fortinet and Halcyon via secondary coverage [S2][S3]. No law enforcement attribution or arrest was found in the sources reviewed.

objectives: Monetary gain through data theft and extortion: the group steals data, lists victims on a leak site and demands payment to suppress release [S2][S3]. It claimed the Grafana Labs intrusion on its leak site and demanded payment to suppress the stolen codebase [S3].

targeting.notes: Tracker data cited by Tech-Insider shows claimed victims clustering most heavily in healthcare, technology and transportation [S8]. Named victims reported by CybelAngel include Vimeo, Vercel, Medtronic, Instructure and Wynn Resort, from a single vendor account [S2]. Leak-site claims include Alpinion, a South Korean medical device company (2026-05) [S5], Integrated Health Systems, a U.S. healthcare provider (2026-08) [S6], and Advanced Engineering Consultants (2026-08) [S7]. Claimed victim totals vary by tracker: about 143 as of 22 June 2026 per Intrinsec, and 207 as of 30 September 2026 per Ransomware.live, as relayed by Tech-Insider [S8]; CybelAngel states 170+ [S2].

capabilities.summary: Vendors describe a data-theft-only model with no encryption payload, pressure applied through a Tor leak site, a 48-hour window to open contact through a negotiation portal and a further 10-day window to pay or renegotiate [S2][S3]. A confirmed intrusion path is the Grafana Labs case, where a compromised GitHub token gave access to the company's GitHub environment and let the attacker download codebase content [S3]. Accounts of the exact Grafana path differ, with one citing a pull_request_target workflow misconfiguration and another a fork of a public repository followed by theft of a privileged token from the runner environment [S3]. Wider claims about infostealer-sourced credentials and initial access brokers appear in search summaries but could not be tied to a dated, openable source and are listed as gaps.

campaigns.name: Leak site debut
campaigns.summary: Vendors report Coinbase Cartel emerged with a new Tor leak site on 15 September 2025, posting roughly ten victims at once [S2].

campaigns.name: Alpinion claim
campaigns.summary: Dexpose reported a 11 May 2026 leak-site claim against Alpinion, a South Korean medical device company [S5].

campaigns.name: Grafana Labs intrusion and extortion
campaigns.summary: The group listed Grafana Labs on its leak site, with sources differing on whether the listing date was 15 or 16 May 2026, shortly before Grafana's public confirmation. Grafana said a stolen GitHub token let an attacker download codebase content, found no impact to customer systems, production environments or personal data, refused to pay and invalidated the token [S2][S3].

campaigns.name: Healthcare and engineering claims
campaigns.summary: Dexpose reported a 22 August 2026 claim against Integrated Health Systems, a U.S. healthcare provider, and SOCRadar reported a 19 August 2026 listing of Advanced Engineering Consultants [S6][S7].

campaigns.name: Victim count growth
campaigns.summary: Ransomware.live counted 207 claimed victims as of 30 September 2026, up from about 143 on 22 June 2026 per Intrinsec, as relayed by Tech-Insider [S8].

diamond.adversary: Financially motivated extortion group branded Coinbase Cartel; Microsoft name Storm-2981 [S1]; vendor-assessed offshoot of the SLSH ecosystem [S2][S3].
diamond.capability: Data theft and extortion without encryption; stolen-token access to code repositories demonstrated against Grafana Labs [S2][S3].
diamond.infrastructure: Tor-based leak site with a negotiation portal [S2]. No domains or IP addresses were found in cited sources.
diamond.victim: Global organizations, clustering in healthcare, technology and transportation [S8]; examples listed in targeting [S2][S5][S6][S7].
diamond.socioPolitical: Criminal profit motive; the Coinbase branding is reported as name only with no tie to the exchange [S2].
diamond.technology: GitHub and source-code hosting environments, with abuse of a stolen token in the Grafana case [S3].

gaps: Microsoft's own reporting on Storm-2981 was not found; the Storm-2981 to Coinbase Cartel link rests on the Microsoft mapping file only [S1].

WebFetch could not reach vendor hosts in this session, so all vendor content comes from search summaries and was not read in full; publication dates of vendor pages were not verified and source dates are approximate to the events they cover.

Claims that about 80 percent of victims show prior infostealer exposure and that the group uses initial access brokers appear in search summaries (Hive Pro, SOCRadar, Infostealers.com, Bitdefender) but were not tied to a verified dated source, so they are not asserted here.
The reported Cognizant listing (15 April 2026, per Lyrie) and the claim that Coinbase Cartel is a rebrand of DataVault are unconfirmed.
Victim counts differ across trackers and the 2023 start-date item conflicts with September 2025 [S3][S8].
Primary documents not opened: Fortinet FortiGuard and Halcyon assessments.
No indicators of compromise, malware names or infrastructure were identified.
Independent searches for Storm-2981 returned no corroborating page; the Storm-2981 to Coinbase Cartel mapping remains unverified.
